title: ALMA and VLA reveal the lukewarm chromospheres of the nearby red supergiants Antares and Betelgeuse
question: Does the red supergiant Antares have a chromosphere detectable at radio wavelengths, and what are its temperature structure and spectral index from ALMA band 8 to VLA S band?

data.bands: ALMA bands 3, 4, 7, 8; VLA S, C, X, Ku, K, Ka, Q

what.value: Photospheric angular diameter of Antares 37.38 mas

evidence.quote: where the diameter of the optical photosphere is 37.38 mas (cite: ohnaka_2013)

what.value: Betelgeuse ALMA/VLA temperature distribution used in revised thermodynamic model

evidence.loc: 4.2 NLTE modeling of the FUV radiation field
evidence.quote: based on the ALMA and VLA temperature distribution shown in Figure 2 of (cite: ogorman_2017)

recipe.method: Model the ionized region with CLEAN, Fourier transform with FT, subtract with UVSUB at S, C, X bands

recipe.goal: Fit size, shape and flux in uv-plane
recipe.method: Fit uniform-intensity circular disks (VLA) and elliptical disks (ALMA) with spectral index free to visibilities
Brightness temperature from flux and diameter equals local gas temperature where optical depth ~1; plotted against radius
assumptions: Optically thick thermal emission; photospheric diameter 37.38 mas

recipe.method: Estimate H- opacity of MOLsphere from CO column density at 2000 K in chemical equilibrium

recipe.goal: NLTE FUV continuum modelling of Betelgeuse
recipe.method: Time-independent NLTE spherical radiative transfer for Si I, Fe I, C I, Mg I continua, with and without Lyα/Lyβ photoionization, compared with STIS radiation temperatures

evidence.loc: 3.1 Size and shape of the Antares atmosphere
evidence.quote: the star deceases in diameter from 68.4 mas (3.7 R$_{\star}$) at 97.5 GHz to 50.7 mas (2.7 R$_{\star}$) at 405 GHz
below 8 GHz the spectral index value is 0.8, while above 20 GHz, the value rises to 1.42
provides a measure of the gas temperature of 2682 $\pm$ 400 K
maximum value of 3777 $\pm$ 567 K at 2.5 R$_{\star}$

evidence.loc: 7 Calculating the optical depth of the MOLsphere
evidence.quote: we obtained an optical depth of $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$
